A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VL-ICL Bench study. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original multimodal ICL evaluations, controlled analyses, and qualitative findings, with detailed numerical results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original evaluations and adds demonstration-selection experiments and an analysis by model architecture in Appendices B.10–B.11.

M1.justification: Appendix B.10 adds an optional context-construction procedure using CLIP embeddings to retrieve top-k demonstrations and arrange them in three orders. This supplements the existing random-selection procedure; the evaluated model architectures, training objectives, and default benchmark remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The ten-task suite and auxiliary VQA, captioning, and text-only evaluations remain. The new selection experiments reuse CLEVR, TextOCR, and CoBSAT. Although v2's separate Matching MiniImageNet Table 23 disappears, that task remains in Figure 10 and v3 Table 53.

E2.justification: v3 adds comparisons between three CLIP-based selection/order variants and random selection in Tables 7–10. The main VLLM roster is unchanged, but the full multi-model Matching MiniImageNet comparison in v2 Table 23 is removed; its two-model chain-of-thought comparison remains.

E3.justification: The added selection study compares most-similar-first, least-similar-first, and shuffled retrieved demonstrations against random selection at 1, 2, 4, and 8 shots. Existing benchmark metrics and settings remain unchanged. Appendix A's new sampling descriptions disclose construction details rather than establish revised experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix B.10 adds a systematic sensitivity study of demonstration selection and ordering across both output modalities, addressing a previously untested factor in ICL performance. B.11 additionally examines architecture families alongside release dates. Existing prompting, context-extension, model-size, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use three random seeds and report averages. Retained detailed tables preserve their uncertainty entries. The new retrieval tables provide point estimates without introducing a different run-count policy, uncertainty estimator, or significance test.

E6.justification: Tables 7–10 add retrieval-condition results: for example, Phi3-Vision's CLEVR peak is 42.0% with retrieval versus 34.5% with random selection. These are new protocol comparisons, not revised same-setting scores. v2 Table 23's separate Matching results are removed; matched retained numerical tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: The conditional-probability formulation of ICL, task definitions, ICL-efficiency definition, and zero-shot/efficiency constraint remain unchanged. Neither version adds a theoretical proof or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: limitations of conventional VQA/captioning evaluations, a diverse multimodal ICL benchmark, and evidence of uneven model capabilities. The added analyses do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: B.10 newly presents demonstration selection as a promising route to improving ICL and claims consistent benefits, although its tables contain exceptions. B.11 concludes that the strongest models are LLaVA-like but finds no general separation between architecture families. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands benchmark-construction documentation across all ten tasks, including source-split sampling, TextOCR filtering and largest-text selection, CoBSAT partitioning, and synthetic counting-image construction. B.10 specifies retrieval modalities and ordering, and the abstract adds a project-page link. These are disclosures, not evidence that the original datasets changed.

R1.justification: B.10 adds positioning around demonstration selection, citing new works by Yuanhan Zhang et al. (2023b), Li et al. (2024c), and Yang et al. (2023), alongside previously cited Chen et al. Most other reference changes update publication metadata, including the attribution of the same GPT-4 technical report.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. v3 adds acknowledgements and appendix subsections, updates the contents list and citation presentation, and makes limited wording corrections, including the Figure 3 caption.

P2.justification: v3 adds four retrieval tables and an architecture-comparison figure, removes v2 Table 23, and relocates the unchanged qualitative Figure 17 as Figure 18. Conference formatting changes headings, headers, and float placement, while existing plots and table designs largely remain.

improvement.justification: The dataset-construction disclosures and new selection controls make the benchmark easier to reproduce and interpret. Benefits are tempered by removal of the full Matching comparison and an overstated retrieval conclusion: Table 10 gives Mantis a CLEVR peak of 40.2% with random selection versus 36.0–36.5% with retrieval. The retained main evidence is unchanged, supporting a limited net improvement.
